answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its votes count, then randomly assign cross-group audits to check whether supposedly independent agents share control. If an audit proves coordinated duplicate identities, their bonds are forfeited and votes removed; auditors earn fees for valid evidence. Sybils remain possible, but an attacker must risk real capital for every identity and cannot cheaply reuse one bond. An orchard registry can mark jade bond tiers and commit audit records to a kernel.
